title: Water corporation interest, asset funding and yard rules
subtitle: Naturalized gardens, municipal alcohol policy, Confederation Park donation, heritage shed demolition and technical rescue retainer fee.
overview: Council directed staff to tell the Province that the Township may be interested in a Water and Wastewater Public Corporation {{vote:m10}}. Staff said the model is not voluntary and the Province may name municipalities that must set one up. Responding keeps the Township involved in shaping the rules, and staff said it does not commit the Township.

Council also supported a request that the Province make the doubled Ontario Community Infrastructure Fund permanent {{vote:m9}}. Staff reported the Township funds about 54% of its optimal asset management target. Council amended the Clean Yards and Property Standards by-laws to permit naturalized gardens under defined standards {{vote:m5}}, and adopted a new Municipal Alcohol Policy for events on Township property {{vote:m6}}.

Council approved an agreement for a private donation to Confederation Park {{vote:m7}}. It approved a heritage permit to demolish a rear shed at 490 Tower Street South {{vote:m4}}. It added a technical rescue retainer fee to the fees by-law {{vote:m8}}. Nothing was reported from the closed session.

decisions.detail: Council directed staff to respond to the Province's Expression of Interest, confirming potential interest in a Water and Wastewater Public Corporation.

decisions.item: Asset management update and OCIF support
decisions.detail: Council received the 2026 asset management update and endorsed the MFOA's request that the doubling of the Ontario Community Infrastructure Fund be made permanent, with staff to send the resolution to the Province.
Council endorsed amendments to the Clean Yards and Property Standards by-laws to allow naturalized gardens under defined maintenance standards.
Council adopted a new policy setting requirements for licensed events on Township property, including insurance, emergency planning and restrictions on higher-risk event types.
Council authorized a Restricted Donation Agreement funding park improvements, including an accessible pathway to be named the Don Watson Trail and Lookout.
Council amended the 2026 fees by-law to add an annual retainer fee for technical rescue services.
Council approved Heritage Permit HP2026-09, which allows demolition of a deteriorated accessory shed at the rear of the designated property.

debate: On the water corporation, one councillor said the benefit to the Township was unclear and worried that major decisions could pass to people without the same care for local water. Staff replied that this was the one chance to help shape the legislation and that regulation could still force the Township to comply.

Councillors asked about debt. Staff said existing water and wastewater debt is expected to stay with the Township, which could reduce its debt capacity. The Province may offer concessions, but staff did not know the details. Staff also did not know how staffing, billing or development charges would work.

Supporters of responding said a medium-sized, growing, non-GTA municipality should be heard, and that a response was described as potential interest that does not lock the Township in. They also compared it to the Township's past engagement on GRCA matters.

On naturalized gardens, a councillor was concerned that neglected yards might be called naturalized. Staff said the by-law keeps the 8-inch height limit and adds objective definitions and conditions on safety, drainage and access.

On Confederation Park, a councillor asked for more community involvement in design and for invasive species removal to be paired with native replanting. Staff proposed an information session and said they would approach local groups.
